description: Theseus kills the Minotaur thanks to Ariadne's thread. But he forgets to change the sails: his father Aegeus throws himself into the sea, which still carries his name.

hero.hook: A monster in a labyrinth. A thread to find the way out. Forgotten sails that give a sea its name.

blocks.text: **Theseus**, the founding hero of Athens, faced the **Minotaur**, a creature half man and half bull hidden in the [[Labyrinth]] of Crete. The story mixes courage, a lover's cunning and family tragedy.
By killing the monster, Theseus freed Athens from a bloody tribute. But one forgotten detail, black sails instead of white ones, would cost his father his life and give the Aegean Sea its name.

King **Minos** of Crete refused to sacrifice a white bull to **Poseidon**, god of the seas. In revenge, Poseidon filled Queen **Pasiphae** with passion for the animal. The Minotaur was born. Minos ordered the inventor [[Daedalus]] to build a prison with no way out: the Labyrinth.

blocks.caption: The Minotaur, shut inside the Cretan Labyrinth

blocks.text: Crete ruled the sea at the time, a [[Thalassocracy]]. After a lost war, Athens had to hand over **seven young men and seven young women** every nine years to feed the monster. At the third delivery, **Theseus**, son of King **Aegeus**, volunteered.
Aegeus and Theseus agreed on a signal: **white** sails if the hero came home alive, **black** sails if he was dead. That detail would decide a tragedy.

sections.title: The Minotaur and the tribute of Athens

blocks.text: In Crete, **Ariadne**, daughter of Minos, fell in love with Theseus. She knew that strength alone is not enough inside the Labyrinth. With help from Daedalus, she gave him a ball of wool: [[Ariadne's thread]]. He tied one end at the entrance and unwound it as he walked.

blocks.caption: Ariadne hands Theseus the thread that will save his life

blocks.text: Theseus killed the Minotaur, then wound the thread back to find the way out. He fled with the young Athenians and with Ariadne. But on the island of **Naxos**, he left her behind while she slept. Some say the god **Dionysus** wanted her for a wife. Ariadne, first in despair and then made divine, received a golden crown that became a constellation.
The homecoming should have been a celebration. Drunk on victory, or shaken by leaving Ariadne, Theseus forgot to raise the white sails. The ship came toward Athens under black canvas.

blocks.caption: Cape Sounion, where Aegeus watched for his son's return

blocks.text: At **Cape Sounion**, the old king Aegeus searched the horizon. All he saw was the black of mourning. Sure that his son was dead, he threw himself off the cliff. The sea has carried his name ever since: the **Aegean Sea**. Theseus landed as a king, and as an orphan through his own carelessness.
The “ship of Theseus” has become a philosophical puzzle: if you replace every plank one by one, is it still the same boat?

sections.title: The black sails off Cape Sounion

blocks.text: Once crowned, Theseus became an organizing king. He is credited with the [[Synoecism]]: the unification of the small towns of Attica around Athens. He founded the [[Panathenaia]], the great festival of the city. Strength joined forces with law.

His reign held other adventures, such as the war against the [[Amazons]]. But the Labyrinth remains his mark: the gift of untangling the impossible, while staying open to a fatal lapse of memory. Theseus built the greatness of Athens on the ashes of a family tragedy.
**Theseus** killed the **Minotaur** thanks to the thread of **Ariadne**. By forgetting to change the sails, he caused the suicide of his father **Aegeus**, who gave his name to the Aegean Sea.
